title.en: Java: the JVM, bytecode and the structure of a program

hook.en: The same Java program runs on Windows, Linux and a phone. The trick is a middle language, bytecode, and a virtual machine on every device that understands it.

objectives.en: Explain the roles of the compiler, bytecode and the JVM
Write, compile and run a simple Java program
Identify the parts of a Java program: class, main, statements, comments

narration.en: The same Java program runs on Windows, Linux and a phone. The trick is a middle language, bytecode, and a virtual machine on every device that understands it.

body.en: Java source code is saved in a .java file. The compiler javac translates it into bytecode, stored in a .class file. Bytecode is not the machine code of any real processor; it is run by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), which interprets it or compiles it just-in-time to native code. Because each platform has its own JVM, the same bytecode runs everywhere: Java is platform independent. The JDK (development kit) contains the compiler and tools; the JRE contains the JVM and libraries needed to run programs.

points.en: JVM runs bytecode on any platform
JDK = tools to develop; JRE = JVM + libraries to run

title.en: On the board: the shape of a Java program

say.en: Every Java program lives in a class. The file name must match a public class.

explanation.en: Source → compiler → bytecode → JVM → output. The JVM checks the bytecode before running it.

body.en: A Java program is built from tokens: keywords (reserved words such as class, int, if, while), identifiers (names you choose: they start with a letter, _ or $, contain no spaces and are case sensitive), literals (constant values: 25, 3.14, 'A', "text", true), operators (+, ==, &&) and separators (; , ( ) { } [ ]). Comments (// single line, /* … */ multi-line, /** … */ documentation) are ignored by the compiler.

points.en: Literals: int, double, char, String, boolean

explanation.en: Identifiers start with a letter, _ or $; may contain digits after the first character; no spaces or hyphens; and cannot be a keyword such as class.
